newsitem.title: USA: NY Pataki calls special legislative session Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: NY Pataki calls special legislative session Dec 17.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki, as expected, on Friday called for a special legislative session that will start on December 17.

The lawmakers will take up at least four issues: reforming how New York City's schools are governed; continuing state taxes that support mass transit in the metropolitan area; extending the New York City income tax surcharge; and extending the current structure for bank taxes.
The governor left open the possibility that he might ask the legislative to approve additional measures.

Before the November elections, Pataki had said he wanted the special session to deal with welfare reform, as the state's system must be changed following the federal reforms signed into law in August. While the Republican governor has submitted his bill, welfare evidently was judged too controversial an issue to be settled quickly.

There has been considerable speculation that the legislators would approve pay increases for themselves, as well as judges and some state officials, but the Senate Majority Leader has said he would be surprised if that were to happen.
And the Assembly Speaker has called for setting up a panel to analyze the issue, according to published reports.
